intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that epidermolysis bullosa simplex-7 with nephropathy and deafness (EBS7) is caused by homozygous mutation in the CD151 gene (602243) on chromosome 11p15.5.

paragraphs.text: Epidermolysis bullosa simplex-7 with nephropathy and deafness (EBS7) is an autosomal recessive disorder. Its features are hereditary nephritis that progresses to end-stage renal disease, pretibial epidermolysis bullosa and sensorineural deafness. Affected individuals have the MER2-negative blood group phenotype.

paragraphs.text: Karamatic Crew et al. (2004) showed that CD151 expresses the MER2 blood group antigen and is present on erythrocytes. It was the first tetraspanin found on red cells. The authors examined CD151 in 3 MER2-negative patients of Indian Jewish origin with end-stage kidney disease, 2 of whom were sibs. All 3 patients were homozygous for a 1-nucleotide insertion (G383) in exon 5 of CD151. The insertion caused a frameshift and a premature stop at codon 140 and was predicted to produce a truncated protein lacking the integrin-binding domain. The authors concluded that CD151 is essential for the proper assembly of glomerular and tubular basement membranes in the kidney and has functional significance in the skin. They also proposed that CD151 is probably a component of the inner ear and could play a role in erythropoiesis.
